title: Poached White Fish Dumplings with Carrot and Beetroot Horseradish
summary: Delicate poached fish dumplings cooked in a fragrant vegetable broth, served chilled with sweet poached carrot and a sharp beetroot horseradish relish on the side.
equipment: large wide pot (at least 5 litres) with lid
small bowl of cold water for your hands

ingredients.item: skinless, boneless white fish fillets (cod, haddock or hake), cut into 3 cm pieces
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
cooked beetroot (not in vinegar), finely grated
prepared horseradish (made with distilled or cider vinegar; check the label)
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Start the Broth
steps.text: Put the water, sliced onion, whole carrots, celery, bay leaf, peppercorns and salt into your largest wide pot and bring to the boil. Lower the heat so it holds at a gentle simmer while you prepare the fish mixture; simmering the vegetables gently draws out their flavour without clouding the broth.

steps.title: Chop the Vegetables
steps.text: Pulse the chopped onion and chopped carrot in a food processor until finely chopped. This fine texture disappears into the mixture as it poaches, adding sweetness and moisture without leaving noticeable chunks.

steps.title: Chop the Fish
steps.text: Add the fish to the processor and pulse in short bursts, scraping down the sides once, until finely chopped but still with a little texture rather than a smooth purée. Keeping some texture is what gives the finished dumplings a light, slightly bouncy bite instead of a dense paste.

steps.title: Mix the Dumpling Mixture
steps.text: Tip everything into a large bowl with the eggs, matzo meal, oil, salt, sugar, white pepper, cold water and dill. Mix well with your hand for about a minute until slightly sticky and evenly combined; the matzo meal and egg bind the mixture so the dumplings hold together as they poach.

steps.title: Test the Seasoning
steps.text: Drop a teaspoon of the mixture into the simmering broth and poach for 4-5 minutes until firm, then taste it and adjust the pepper or dill in the remaining mixture as needed, since it's already well salted. Testing a small piece first means you can fix the seasoning before committing the whole batch.

steps.title: Shape the Dumplings
steps.text: With wet hands, shape the mixture into 12 ovals, each about 8 x 5 cm and roughly 90 g, wetting your hands between each one. Damp hands stop the sticky mixture clinging to your fingers and help you form a smooth, even surface.

steps.title: Poach Gently
steps.text: Lower the dumplings into the barely simmering broth with a slotted spoon in a single layer, cooking in two batches if the pot feels crowded. Cover and simmer very gently, with just the occasional bubble, for 25-30 minutes until firm and cooked through, reaching at least 71°C in the centre, which matters because the mixture contains egg. A rolling boil would be too rough and can break the dumplings apart.

steps.title: Cool and Slice
steps.text: Lift out the dumplings and the whole carrots onto a dish, spoon over a little broth, then cool before covering and chilling for at least 2 hours, or serve warm if you prefer. Once cool, slice the carrots into 5 mm coins; chilling firms up the dumplings and lets the flavours settle.

steps.title: Make the Relish and Serve
steps.text: Mix the grated beetroot, horseradish, cider vinegar, sugar and salt together and chill. Top each dumpling with a carrot coin and serve two per person with a spoonful of the beetroot horseradish alongside, its sharp, peppery bite cutting nicely through the mild, delicate fish.

tips: Don't over-process the fish into a smooth paste — a little texture is what keeps the dumplings light rather than dense.
Always poach a test spoonful first so you can adjust the seasoning before shaping the whole batch.
A common mistake is letting the broth boil hard once the dumplings are in; keep it at a bare simmer or they can break apart.
Chilling the dumplings before serving firms up the texture and makes them easier to slice and serve neatly.
storage: Cool and store the dumplings in their broth, covered, in the fridge for up to 3 days, or freeze without the relish for up to 2 months. Thaw in the fridge overnight, and if serving warm, reheat gently in their broth until piping hot (74°C); otherwise serve well chilled. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
